Distraction Maze

Find your way from the blue dot to the gold star as quickly as you can, without bumping into walls.

You'll play two rounds on mazes of equal difficulty: first with no distractions, then with sounds, pop-ups, moving shapes and stray thoughts. At the end you'll compare the two.

Controls: arrow keys or W A S D. On a phone or tablet, use the arrow buttons under the maze or swipe on the maze.

🎧 Turn your sound on — audio is part of the experience. This activity includes moving shapes and pop-ups but no rapid flashing.
This is a classroom awareness activity, not a clinical or diagnostic tool, and it can only hint at what living with ADHD is like. Adapted from ADHD_simulator by sayanthsai (CC0), including its original audio.

Round 1 done ✅

Round 2 is a maze of the same size and difficulty (the same layout, mirrored). This time, distractions will start shortly after you begin. Try to stay focused on the maze.

Your results

Reflect

  1. What did you notice about your attention when the distractions started? Which kind pulled you away most — sounds, pop-ups, moving shapes, or the "thoughts"?
  2. Did you click the flashing button or read the notifications, even though they didn't help you finish? Why do you think that happened?
  3. How might it feel if these interruptions came from inside your own head and you couldn't switch them off at the end of the activity?
  4. What could a teacher, classmate, or workplace change to make a task like this easier for someone who is easily distracted?
